narrative.text: French summaries of 2002 Bulletin of the World Health Organization articles, beginning with trials in Viet Nam comparing a locally produced bivalent oral cholera vaccine with a commercial one in adults and children. The local vaccine was judged safe and immunogenic, even without buffer and in children. The page also includes fragments of an abstract on factors behind variation in US mortality rates; the two-column layout makes the extracted text jumbled.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, starting with a Seychelles study that used electronic pill boxes to track one-year adherence to antihypertensive treatment after population screening, finding low adherence that improved with regular follow-up. Adherence was linked to skilled occupations, health awareness and attendance, and inversely to heavy drinking. The page ends with part of an abstract on an environmental hygiene indicator for Ascaris infection risk in children.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, including an economic evaluation of in-service midwifery training programmes in South Kalimantan, Indonesia, giving marginal costs per 1% increase in competent midwives. Another abstract models mother-to-child HIV prevention and antiretroviral use, warning that drug resistance could reach 25–100% of cases after 30 years. The two abstracts are interleaved in the extraction.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, beginning with a review of evidence on whether health and nutrition cause economic prosperity, noting that trials show iron deficiency lowers work capacity while observational links are harder to interpret. The authors call for longer socioeconomic surveys and trials measuring economic effects. The page ends with an abstract on ethics guidance and bioethics capacity for equity-oriented health research.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, including one on how patents on research tools such as gene sequences may slow medical research and complicate preferential pricing for developing countries, with possible responses. Another reviews global responses to antimicrobial resistance and proposes ways to strengthen collective international action.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, beginning with a review of community health financing for rural and informal-sector workers in Africa and Asia, finding it improves access and financial protection. It sets out five government options such as targeted subsidies and reinsurance. A second abstract discusses public expenditure management needed in heavily indebted poor countries receiving debt relief.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, including a review of trade in health services under the General Agreement on Trade in Services, describing mixed effects on equity, efficiency, quality and access and proposing policies on brain drain and public–private links. Another reports low prevalence but high risk behaviour for reproductive tract infections in rural Bangladesh, calling for primary prevention.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, beginning with an assessment of five infectious disease surveillance and response systems in the United Republic of Tanzania in 1998. It found that apart from the health management information system they were rarely present, with few standard case definitions and weak reporting and supervision. The page ends with an estimate showing a low risk of vaccine-associated paralytic polio in India.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, beginning with a district-level audit of 130 maternal deaths in South Kalimantan, Indonesia, mainly from haemorrhage and hypertensive disorders. It found that delayed decisions and poor care contributed to most deaths and that the audit improved obstetric care. The page ends with an abstract on questionnaires for rapid assessment of schistosomiasis.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, including a review of economic analyses of rubella and rubella vaccines that found favourable benefit–cost ratios and supported introducing the vaccine in developing countries. Another abstract reports that universal infant vaccination in South Africa with low-dose, low-cost plasma-derived hepatitis B vaccine was highly effective.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, beginning with models of child wasting prevalence in Africa, Latin America and Asia, finding low birth weight to be the main common predictor and linking it to women's status. The page also includes an abstract on gender inequality in cataract surgery coverage, calling for interventions to reach women.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, including an estimate that human rabies deaths in the United Republic of Tanzania are heavily under-reported, with about 1 500 deaths a year predicted from active bite surveillance against about 11 officially recorded. Another abstract examines whether laboratory containment of wild polioviruses after eradication is feasible.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, including a critical look at indicators of met need for obstetric care. Another reviews options for influencing the private health sector in low-income countries, given concerns about care quality for TB, malaria and STIs. The page ends with the methods of a study evaluating WHO's epidemic threshold strategy for meningococcal meningitis in Africa.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, reporting that WHO's epidemic threshold for meningococcal meningitis in seven African countries in 1997 had high sensitivity and specificity, and that timely vaccination cut cases in one district by about 60%. The page also introduces a retrospective study of ectopic pregnancy in Conakry, Guinea. It ends with a case-control study linking education level to cardiovascular risk factors.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, beginning with a community study of epilepsy in rural Gambia that found a large treatment gap, beliefs in supernatural causes and demand for preventive treatment. It suggests integrating epilepsy into chronic disease programmes. The page ends with part of a modelling study on how long mass ivermectin treatment is needed to eliminate onchocerciasis.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, concluding the onchocerciasis modelling study, which found elimination feasible in most African foci but possibly requiring prohibitive duration and coverage in highly endemic areas. It then summarizes a study of mortality trends and spatial distribution among children aged 12–60 months in São Paulo, Brazil, from 1980 to 1998.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, beginning with an evaluation of two years of quarterly mass albendazole treatment in rural Hamadan province, Iran, which cut Ascaris infection from 53% to 6%. A review of air travel and venous thromboembolism concludes that a link probably exists. The page ends with proposed comparable measures of reproductive health.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, including the role of the International Council for the Control of Iodine Deficiency Disorders in the global partnership for universal salt iodization. Another reviews ten years of the DOTS strategy for tuberculosis in China. A third begins a cost-effectiveness comparison of community health workers in TB control in Bangladesh.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, reporting that the BRAC community health worker TB programme in Bangladesh achieved similar cure rates to the government programme at a third lower cost per patient cured. Another abstract describes adapting DOTS for displaced people in Churachandpur, India, amid conflict and an HIV epidemic. The page ends with lessons from China's DOTS experience.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, including WHO's view on broadening operational research for TB control and the barriers to DOTS expansion, such as weak political commitment, drug supply problems, HIV and drug resistance. It continues the list of lessons from China's DOTS programme. It ends with a summary on how molecular typing has advanced TB epidemiology.

French summaries of Bulletin articles, beginning with a review of new tuberculosis vaccine development, noting that over 100 candidates exist and the most promising are entering human safety trials. Another sets out a framework for managing multidrug-resistant TB and access to costly drugs, discussing WHO's DOTS-Plus working group and the need to strengthen basic DOTS first.
